component.name: Immich Folder Watch
component.summary: Watch folders and upload new media to Immich

description.p: Immich Folder Watch monitors local folders and automatically uploads new photos and videos to your Immich server. It runs as a per-user desktop app with full Wayland and X11 support, talking to Immich over its public HTTP API rather than touching the server's storage directly.

ul.li: Automatically upload screenshots into a dedicated Immich album.
Watch a DSLR or SD-card import folder and send new photos through.
Ingest scanner output into a family archive.
Pick up files dropped by another tool into a staging folder.
Per-folder sync modes: upload only new files, upload everything in the folder, or keep the folder bidirectionally in sync with its Immich album (additive — local files are never deleted).
Optional per-folder album placement; missing albums are created automatically.
Waits until files are fully written before upload; retries transient failures.
Realtime status via Socket.IO; live tray status (where the desktop supports it).
English and German UI with OS auto-detection and live language switching.

screenshot.caption: Settings: Immich server, watch sources, per-folder sync mode, and autostart

description.p: The first Linux release of Immich Folder Watch. Avalonia GUI on Wayland and X11, full feature parity with the Windows tray app: watch sources, batch upload, per-folder sync modes, album-rename propagation, Socket.IO realtime, and English/German UI with OS auto-detect.

ul.li: D-Bus FileChooser portal for picking watch sources, with host-path resolution via the Documents portal.
Polling sweep alongside FileSystemWatcher so inotify-blind FUSE doc-portal mounts still detect new files and deletions.
StatusNotifierItem tray on KDE Plasma and on GNOME with the AppIndicator extension; window-only banner fallback otherwise.
Background-portal opt-in (GNOME 46+) so closing the window keeps the worker running.
journald log target as the Linux default, with a File option for rolling on-disk logs.
Hidden-window autostart and a clean uninstall path.

description.p: Windows MSI behavior is unchanged from 2.4.0 — same installer, same Event Log integration, same upgrade path.
